To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fixed‐dose combinations of RAAS blockers and diuretics are effective in achieving BP goals in patients with hypertension and are well tolerated.

the combination of an RAAS blocking agent with a diuretic is more effective than the combination of an angiotensinaldosterone system blocking agent with a calcium channel blocker for lowering blood pressure.
the use of fixed‐dose combinations of antihypertensives has been shown to improve BP control, reduce cardiovascular events, and improve medication adherence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of RAAS blockers in combination with diuretics and calcium channel blockers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

fixed‐dose combinations of RAAS blockers/diuretics or RAAS blockers/calcium channel blockers are effective and well‐tolerated initial antihypertension therapy, and that the use of these combinations is associated with improved adherence and better BP control than the use of single‐component agents.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fixed‐dose combinations of RAAS blockers and thiazide diuresis are effective for lowering BP and may be preferable to individual components of these drugs.
the combination of a diuretic and RAAS blocker is the best approach for the initial management of hypertension.
combination therapy has been used successfully for decades.
The main takeaway from our work is that
combination therapy is necessary in a large number of people with hypertension and that RAAS blockers are useful components of combination therapy.
the combination of an RAAS blocking agent with a diuretic or calcium channel blocker provides the best chance for patients to achieve BP goals.
combination therapy is a reasonable strategy in many patients with hypertension, and the choice of the combination should be individualized based on comorbid conditions.
